title: Linear approximation
goal: Estimate a tough number (like $\sqrt{101}$ or $\ln(1.05)$) without a calculator by riding the tangent line $L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)$ from a nearby easy anchor $a$.

beforeThis.skill: Linear approximation is nothing new—$L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)$ is literally just the tangent line equation at $x = a$ with a new name!

seeIt.title: Linear Approximation
seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Shows how the tangent line $L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)$ estimates values of $f(x)$ near $x = a$ (with the chapter overview in 3Blue1Brown at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3d6DsjIBzJ4).

slowWalkthrough.title: Calculus 2 Lecture 9.9: Approximation of Functions by Taylor Polynomials
slowWalkthrough.creator: Professor Leonard

questions.asking: See which of $f(5)$, $f'(5)$, and $f(0)$ can be known exactly from the linear approximation $f(x) \approx 3x - 9$ centered at $x = 5$.
questions.statement:
Suppose $f(x)$ is a function, and we calculated its linear approximation near $x = 5$ to be $f(x) \approx 3x - 9$.

  1. What is $f(5)$?
  2. What is $f'(5)$?
  3. What is $f(0)$?

questions.asking: Estimate $\log(0.93)$ using the tangent line to $f(x) = \log x$ at $a = 1$, and sketch the curve and tangent line.
questions.statement:
Use a linear approximation to estimate $\log(x)$ when $x = 0.93$. Sketch the curve $y = f(x)$ and your linear approximation.

(Remember we use $\log x$ to mean the natural logarithm of $x$, $\log_e x$.)

questions.asking: Estimate $\sqrt[5]{30}$ using a linear approximation of $f(x) = \sqrt[5]{x}$ at a nearby point where the fifth root is an integer.
